ctx.x: Did he play that type of bass sometimes, like the Pine Top bass or any of those Boogie Woogie basses? Did he use that style?

Well, in fact, I never noticed him playing the style of Boogie Woogie. Boogie Woogie is really originally run by a fella that they called him Burmanham. And during the time, there was good friends Burmanham, Jell-O-Roll, and they hired Black Peaks. Well, the fellas used to play blues. Now the first really the top originator of Boogie Woogie that I ever know of, the first one. But he left here. Then he went to Scarborough. Oh, he was a big man. And there was Albert Ambers. Albert Ambers? Ambers. Ambers. Ambers.

Ambers. You remember when he died? Remember when he died, you told me you met him up on Beale Street once, huh? Is that the same fella? I came over and told you about him dying. You said you met him on Beale Street once. Is that the same fella? When I was taking lessons from you. No. What did it take for?
